expectations.text: Detects Python/Django from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml
expectations.evidence: wiki.config.yaml sets stack.language=python, stack.framework=django, stack.framework_version='>=4.2', build_files=[requirements.txt, manage.py]. detection-trace.md Phase 1 documents scanning requirements.txt (containing 'Django>=4.2', 'djongo', 'pymongo') plus manage.py stub verifying DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE.

wiki.config.yaml ecosystem.orm.profiles=['django'] with detected_entities listing {class: Article, file: myapp/models.py, db_table: articles}. detection-trace.md Phase 2 cites 'class Article(models.Model):' matching the django.yaml entity_class regex and db_table='articles' override.

wiki.config.yaml ecosystem.database: {enabled: true, driver: mongodb, connector: djongo, environments.default: {engine: djongo, name: mydb, host: mongodb://localhost:27017, source: myapp/settings.py}} with guard-rail policy (block_ddl, block_privilege, dml_mode: present_only) and audit enabled. detection-trace.md Phase 3 cites djongo ENGINE and mongodb:// URI scheme as the two independent indicators.

File exists at outputs/wiki.config.yaml (3843 bytes) and parses as valid YAML via js-yaml. All required top-level sections present: wiki, stack, ecosystem (agents/credentials/database/orm/claude_md/mermaid), autonomy, sources, lint, claims, security, code_locality, refresh, graph, cache, logging, hooks, hooks_always_on, multimodal. Stack and ecosystem values align with fixture (python/django/mongodb/djongo).

outputs/wiki-scaffold/ contains the full directory set created by init_wiki.ts: wiki/ (with index.md, summaries.md, overview.md, claims/, synthesis/, templates/), graph/ (edges.jsonl), log/ (events.jsonl, daily/), audit/, raw/, outputs/, .wiki-cache/, plus .wiki-ignore and .claude/settings.json with the PreToolUse hooks installed.

claims.claim: Only one ORM entity was detected (Article -> articles)
claims.evidence: events.jsonl: entities_detected=1; wiki.config.yaml detected_entities lists a single Article class with db_table=articles, matching the trace's myapp/models.py walk.

claims.claim: djongo is the Django+MongoDB connector and was identified via both requirements.txt and settings.py ENGINE
claims.evidence: detection-trace.md Phase 3 cross-references djongo in requirements.txt with ENGINE='djongo' in settings.py DATABASES; pymongo presence in requirements.txt is consistent.

claims.claim: No external source agents were enabled due to non-interactive eval
claims.evidence: wiki.config.yaml ecosystem.agents.source={} and events.jsonl sources_enabled=[]; trace Phase 4 documents the conservative default.

claims.claim: Claude Code PreToolUse hooks were installed during scaffold
claims.evidence: wiki-scaffold/.claude/settings.json (978 bytes) exists alongside the scaffold directories, matching trace Phase 6.

suggestions.reason: Assertion only checks driver=mongodb. Consider also verifying the guard-rail policy stanza (dml_mode, block_ddl, audit.enabled) is present — those are the load-bearing parts of 'configures the database agent', and a config with just driver=mongodb but no policy would still pass today.

Passes on directory existence alone. A discriminating version would check that seed files (wiki/index.md, graph/edges.jsonl, log/events.jsonl) and the .claude/settings.json hook wiring exist — otherwise an empty directory tree satisfies the assertion.

No assertion verifies the detected ORM entity (Article -> articles table). The trace and config both record this; an assertion like 'at least one Django entity extracted with db_table mapping' would catch silent regressions in the orm extractor.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions pass cleanly and the eval is structurally sound, but a few check presence rather than substance. Tightening the DB-agent and scaffold assertions would make them more discriminating.
